title: Steve Coach Report - Mar 16
summary: Live coaching review of CORNER build. Two passes: initial C3 review (C+), then updated grades after Bobby's single-image pivot and GameHUD ship.
content:
CORNER Coach Report: March 16, 2026

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead / Product Coach) Reference: Product spec v1.3 (THE BIBLE), Steffen's visual-target/notes.md, full-office-warm-night.png (north star)

PASS 2: Updated Grades (post-commits e8344d3, 7ff7800, ece69dc, 4d2ebe3)

Bobby read the coach report and made a smart architectural decision: instead of compositing 14 individual room PNGs into the building shell (which required transparent backgrounds from Steffen), he used the full-office-warm-night.png as a SINGLE cohesive background image with interactive click targets overlaid on top. This is the right call. One image, one building, no seams.

1. VISUAL COMPOSITION -- Grade: B+ (was C+)

What changed: The IsometricOffice component now renders full-office-warm-night.png as one 880x880 image. No more CSS grid of separate room tiles. No more gaps. No more dark hexagonal borders. The building IS the north star image.

What's working now:

  • Connected building. Shared walls, starfield, ground plane, CORNER sign, window light spill. All present because they're baked into Steffen's render. This was the #1 problem and it's solved.
  • Interactive overlays aligned. IMAGE_ROOM_TARGETS maps each room to percentage-based click targets. Commit 4d2ebe3 refined these positions with row/col comments. Nameplates, status dots, and hover highlights sit on top of the image at the correct room positions.
  • Camera system still works. Zoom, pan (with momentum), pinch-to-zoom on mobile, camera centering on room click. All carried over cleanly from the grid approach.
  • Atmosphere layers added. Warm radial gradient (top-left), cool radial gradient (bottom-right), vignette overlay. Subtle but they add depth.
  • pointer-events: none on the image. Smart. The image doesn't intercept clicks. Only the explicit target divs do. Commit 7ff7800 fixed this.

What's NOT working:

  • Static image means no per-room dynamic state. When Bobby is WORKING, his room should glow differently than when he's IDLE. With individual room tiles, you could swap images or overlay colored gradients per room. With a single static image, per-room visual state is limited to the overlay divs (border highlight + status dot). The status dots are there but the room ITSELF doesn't change. Bobby's purple LED doesn't pulse when he's active because it's baked into the PNG.
  • Zoom beyond 2x starts to pixelate. The image is 1024x1024 rendered at 880px. At 3.5x zoom (the max), you're effectively viewing it at ~3000px. Quality holds until about 2x, then softens. For the detail zoom level, Bobby might need a 2048x2048 variant of the image, or Steffen should deliver a higher-res version.
  • Room click targets are percentage-based approximations. They work but aren't pixel-perfect. Some rooms have targets that slightly overlap or don't cover the room's full visual area. This is inherent to the approach: a static image doesn't have DOM boundaries per room. The 4d2ebe3 refinement improved alignment but it's still manual tuning.

Why B+ and not A: The single-image approach is brilliant for getting the visual right quickly. It LOOKS like the north star because it IS the north star. But it trades visual dynamism for static beauty. The A-grade version would have the building come alive: rooms brightening/dimming based on agent state, light spilling differently at night vs day, Bobby's purple LED pulsing when he's active. That requires either (a) compositing individual rooms with state-based overlays on top of the shell, or (b) generating multiple full-office variants (active-bobby, active-elon, etc.) and transitioning between them. Neither is urgent. The current approach ships a product that looks great. Dynamic state is C4 territory.

Remaining action items:

  1. Get a 2048x2048 version of full-office-warm-night.png from Steffen for high-zoom detail level.
  2. Add per-room glow overlays. The click target divs already have hover/selected states. Add a persistent glow for WORKING status: a radial gradient inside the target div at 10-15% opacity using the agent's color. This makes active rooms visually pop without replacing the image.
  3. Consider a "daytime" variant of the full-office image for time-of-day switching. Steffen already has a golden-hour visual target. Using it based on the user's local time would be delightful.

2. GAME HUD (Bobby 2, commit e8344d3) -- Grade: B+

The Sims x Chaart vision: does it match?

Yes, substantially. This is a genuinely good HUD implementation. Let me break it down against the spec.

What's working:

  • Bottom strip, 48px. Patrik said "compact strip that doesn't cover the game." This delivers. 48px on desktop, 44px on mobile. Fixed to the bottom edge. The game viewport is never occluded by the HUD.
  • Project pills, not agent pills. Patrik said "real tasks grouped by project." The HUD parses punch-list.md (via local API) and groups tasks into projects: Today, Ambition, AOM Phase 2, AI Advisory, Outreach, Client Deadlines, Infrastructure, This Week. Color-coded, with task counts and micro progress bars. This is exactly what was asked for.
  • Expand on demand. Click a project pill, a 320px-max panel slides up ABOVE the strip (not dropping down from the top). Shows the project's tasks with checkboxes, agent avatars, done/pending sorting. Close on click outside or Escape. This is the right UX: quick glance without leaving the game.
  • Agent dot grid (Sims-style). Sorted by activity (WORKING first, BLOCKED second, etc.). Sprite avatars clipped circular with status border colors. Pulse ring on active agents. Red X on blocked agents. Click any dot to zoom to that room. This reads as "Sims household panel" more than anything else in the entire build.
  • Quick stats. Active count (green), blocked count (red), done count (blue), AZ time, overall progress arc (SVG donut). JetBrains Mono monospace. This is the Chaart side of the baby: clean data density.
  • Code quality. Lazy loaded, code-split from GameDashboard. Does not touch GameDashboard internals. Clean separation. usePunchListData hook with local/production fallback. Polls at 5s locally, 60s in production. Click-outside dismiss. Escape key handler. Mobile responsive (hides agent grid, shrinks to 44px).

What's NOT working:

P0: Z-index collision with ChatBar. GameHUD is fixed to bottom:0 at z:40. ChatBar is also fixed to bottom:0 at z:30. On desktop, the GameHUD renders ON TOP of the ChatBar's collapsed 56px strip. The chat input is hidden behind the HUD. This is a critical layering bug. The ChatBar (56px) and GameHUD (48px) are fighting for the same pixel space.

Fix: One of two approaches:

  • (a) Stack them. ChatBar at bottom:0, GameHUD at bottom:56 (above the chat bar). Total bottom UI height: 104px. Might feel heavy.
  • (b) Merge them. The GameHUD IS the bottom bar. Chat input lives inside the HUD strip (left section: agent avatar + input, center: project pills, right: stats). One strip, not two. This is cleaner and matches the "compact" directive better. The current ChatBar's collapsed state is essentially just an input field with an agent avatar. That can live inside the HUD.

P1: Production mode fallback is empty. When not on localhost, usePunchListData falls back to the status API but returns null (no punch-list parsing for production data). The HUD shows "No punch list data." For the demo, this means the HUD is empty on aheadofmarket.com. Need either: (a) a static demo data set, or (b) parse agent status data into project groups as a fallback.

P2: Punch-list parser is brittle. It pattern-matches on specific section header text ("## TODAY", "## AMBITION", "## AOM SITE"). If the punch-list.md format changes (and it does, frequently), the parser breaks silently. Consider adding a "## PROJECTS" section to punch-list with structured YAML-like headers, or use a separate punch-list-projects.json that's machine-readable.

Is it compact enough? Yes. 48px is one line of content. The pills scroll horizontally. The expand-on-click pattern means the strip stays thin until you need detail. This matches the Sims green diamond bar: always there, never in the way, click for more.

Are the tasks real? On localhost, yes. It parses the actual punch-list.md with real projects, real task checkboxes, real agent assignments. The "Ambition" pill shows Ambition tasks. The "AI Advisory" pill shows GTM tasks. This is genuinely useful.

Specific action items:

  1. Fix z-index collision. ChatBar and GameHUD cannot both own bottom:0. Merge the chat input into the GameHUD, or stack them with explicit spacing.
  2. Add production fallback data. Even a hardcoded demo project list is better than "No punch list data."
  3. Add keyboard shortcut. 'H' to toggle HUD visibility. Match the 'T' shortcut pattern from the old TaskHUD.

3. CHAT WIRING (Bobby 3, commits 7ff7800 + ece69dc) -- Grade: B+

What changed: The local chat now works end-to-end through the Telegram relay pipeline. This is significant.

The flow (localhost):

  1. User types in ChatBar, hits send.
  2. ChatBar calls POST /api/local/relay-send with { agent, message, source: 'corner-dashboard' }.
  3. The Vite dev server handler writes to relay-inbox.jsonl with { id, agent, message, status: 'pending', chat_id, timestamp }.
  4. The EA hook (relay-hook.sh) picks up the pending message on the next user prompt.
  5. EA processes it and responds via relay-respond.py, which writes to relay-outbox.jsonl.
  6. ChatBar polls /api/local/relay-outbox?since=timestamp every 2 seconds.
  7. When a response appears (from EA, not from dashboard's own sends), it displays in the chat.

What's working:

  • Both HTTP and WebSocket paths go to the same place. Commit ece69dc fixed the WebSocket handler to write to relay-inbox (not outbox). Both transport layers now use the same pipeline. Clean.
  • Relay polling with deduplication. startRelayPoll tracks lastOutboxCheckRef so it doesn't replay old messages. Filters out messages from 'corner-dashboard' and 'corner-websocket' sources. Only shows EA responses.
  • Error handling. If the relay-send fails, the chat shows a "Failed to send" error in the assistant bubble. Not silent failure.
  • Auto-cleanup. relayPollRef interval is cleared on unmount and before starting a new poll. No leaked timers.

What's NOT working:

The chat only works when the EA main session is actively running. The relay-inbox message sits there until the EA's hook fires on the next user prompt. If Patrik isn't actively using the terminal session, the chat message could wait indefinitely. This is inherent to the relay architecture (it's designed for Telegram, not real-time chat). For real-time chat, the C4 WebSocket-to-CC bridge is needed.

No "waiting for response" timeout. The relay poll runs every 2 seconds with no timeout. If the EA never responds (session crashed, compacted, whatever), the chat shows a permanent "..." streaming indicator. Add a 60-second timeout that replaces the streaming bubble with "No response. The assistant may be busy or offline."

agentSlug in startRelayPoll closure is stale. The updateMessages call inside the poll interval captures agentSlug from the closure at the time startRelayPoll was called. If the user switches agents while waiting for a response, the response could update the wrong agent's message history. Minor but worth noting.

Specific action items:

  1. Add a 60-second timeout to the relay poll. Show a "No response" message rather than infinite spinner.
  2. Capture agentSlug as a parameter to startRelayPoll instead of relying on closure.
  3. Add a visual indicator in the chat when the EA session isn't running (localhost check: try to read a heartbeat file or status endpoint).

4. TOP TASK HUD (unchanged) -- Grade: B-

The old TaskHUD (top bar with drawer) is still present and unchanged. It still has the dropdown overlay problem. But with GameHUD now handling the "project pills + task list" at the bottom, the top bar's role is simplified: CORNER logo, mode switcher, local/WS badges. The drawer content (Session/Project/Upcoming/Add tabs) is largely superseded by GameHUD's project pills.

Recommendation: Remove the drawer from the top TaskHUD entirely. Keep it as a pure navigation bar: logo (left), mode switcher (center), zoom controls or settings (right). The bottom GameHUD handles all task/project data. Having two HUDs with overlapping purposes confuses the hierarchy.

5. STEFFEN'S ASSETS -- Grade: A- (unchanged)

Steffen's deliverables haven't changed since Pass 1. The grade holds. However, Bobby's single-image approach reduces the urgency of several Steffen action items:

  • Transparent room PNGs: NO LONGER NEEDED for the main view. Bobby uses the full-office image directly. Individual room PNGs are still useful for the room detail sidebar or zoom-to-room view, but they're not blocking the main visual.
  • Compositing spec: PARTIALLY MOOT. The single-image approach bypasses CSS compositing. What IS still needed: room click target coordinates. Bobby is manually tuning percentage values. Steffen could provide a coordinate map derived from the image composition.
  • HUD reference images: STILL NEEDED. Bobby built the GameHUD without visual references and it turned out well, but Steffen should still provide mockups for the next iteration (merged chat+HUD bar, project pill design refinement).
  • Higher-res full-office image: NEW NEED. 2048x2048 for the detail zoom level.

6. OVERALL PRODUCT STATE -- Grade: B (was C+)

Jump from C+ to B in one session. The single-image pivot was the highest-leverage decision Bobby could have made. Instead of spending days compositing individual rooms with transparent backgrounds and CSS clip paths (which required Steffen to re-export 14 PNGs), he used the finished visual target as the actual product. The north star IS the product. That's smart.

What the demo communicates now:

  • "This is a real office with real rooms. The building has character." (Visual composition: achieved.)
  • "I can see my projects and their progress at a glance." (GameHUD: achieved on localhost.)
  • "I can chat with any agent." (Chat wiring: achieved on localhost.)
  • "The system knows what's happening." (Agent status dots, minimap, mode switching: achieved.)

What it still doesn't communicate:

  • "The building is alive." Rooms don't change based on agent state. The image is static. This is the last visual hurdle.
  • "I can use this instead of the terminal." Chat only works when the EA terminal session is running. No standalone mode yet (C4).
  • "This is polished enough to show clients." The z-index collision (HUD covering chat) and the lack of production fallback data would confuse anyone who isn't on localhost.

Updated Priority Stack:

Priority Item Owner Impact Status
1 Integrate building shell Bobby 10x visual quality DONE (single-image approach)
2 Transparent room PNGs Steffen Unblock compositing BYPASSED (not needed for single-image)
3 Compositing spec Steffen Build target for Bobby BYPASSED
1 (NEW) Fix z-index collision (GameHUD covering ChatBar) Bobby Critical usability bug. Chat is unusable on desktop.
2 (NEW) Merge ChatBar into GameHUD or stack them explicitly Bobby + Steffen One bottom strip, not two competing strips.
3 Add per-room glow overlays for WORKING state Bobby Makes the building feel alive. Quick win.
4 Production fallback data for GameHUD Bobby HUD works on aheadofmarket.com demo.
5 Remove top TaskHUD drawer (keep navbar only) Bobby Eliminates redundant task UI. Cleaner hierarchy.
6 2048x2048 full-office image for detail zoom Steffen Crisp at high zoom.
7 Chat relay timeout (60s) Bobby No more infinite loading spinners.
8 Wire chat streaming to sprite state Bobby Chat feels connected to the world.

What's Impressive (this session)

Bobby shipped 4 commits in under 10 minutes (e8344d3, 7ff7800, ece69dc, 4d2ebe3). The GameHUD is 705 lines of production-quality React with real data parsing, responsive design, accessibility (keyboard shortcuts, click-outside-to-close), code splitting, and graceful fallbacks. The punch-list parser handles multiple markdown section formats including tables. The relay chat wiring correctly routes through the same pipeline as Telegram messages, with proper source tagging to avoid echo loops.

The single-image pivot shows architectural maturity. Bobby recognized that perfecting CSS compositing of 14 room images was a multi-day yak-shave when the finished visual already existed as a single PNG. Ship the image. Overlay the interactivity. Move on.

GRADE HISTORY

Component Pass 1 Pass 2 Delta
Visual Composition C+ B+ +2 steps
Task HUD (top) B- B- unchanged
Game HUD (bottom) n/a B+ NEW
Chat Bar B B+ +0.5 step
Steffen Assets A- A- unchanged
OVERALL C+ B +1.5 steps

WHAT IT TAKES TO HIT A

Three things:

  1. Fix the bottom bar. Merge ChatBar and GameHUD into one unified strip. Chat input on the left, project pills in the center, agent dots + stats on the right. One bar. 56px. Done. This alone turns the bottom half of the screen from "two things competing" to "one elegant control center."

  2. Per-room glow. When Bobby is WORKING, his room area in the game gets a subtle purple radial gradient overlay at 10-15% opacity. When Elon is WORKING, green. This makes the building feel alive without replacing the static image. The click target divs already exist at the right positions. Just add a background gradient when the status is WORKING. 20 lines of code.

  3. Production demo data. The GameHUD showing "No punch list data" on aheadofmarket.com is a non-starter for demos. Hard-code a representative project list (4-5 projects, 15-20 tasks, mix of done/pending) that shows what the HUD looks like with real content. This is the "polished enough to show clients" threshold.

Those three items turn B into A. The architecture is there. The visual is there. These are finishing moves.

7. BREATHING ANIMATION + SPEAKING WIRE (commit 049a0d4) -- Quick Review

Breathing float: 3px sine wave, 5s cycle. Nested wrapper so it doesn't conflict with zoom/pan transforms. This is a good micro-interaction. The building feels alive and resting. Patrik asked for it, Bobby delivered in one commit. The implementation is correct: separate inner div with the animation, outer div handles transforms.

onSpeaking callback wired: ChatBar now accepts an onSpeaking prop. When streaming=true, it calls up to set streamingAgent. The state exists and the AgentCharacterHTML component knows how to use it (getSpriteState checks isSpeaking). BUT: the IsometricOffice component in single-image mode doesn't render AgentCharacterHTML components. The characters are part of the PNG. So the speaking sprite swap doesn't happen visually.

This is the key trade-off of the single-image approach: you get perfect visual composition but lose per-agent sprite state. To solve this, Bobby could:

  • Layer individual agent sprite images ON TOP of the full-office image at each room's position. When an agent is speaking, swap the sprite from idle to speaking. The background remains the static image, but the character changes.
  • This requires Steffen to provide a version of the full-office image WITHOUT characters (just rooms + furniture), and individual character sprites at the correct position and scale for each room.

Not urgent. The wiring is there for when the architecture supports it. Good forward-thinking.

PASS 3: GameHUD v2 + ChatBar v2 (commits 897fac9, a5bc5f2)

Two more commits just landed. Bobby is moving fast.

8. GAME HUD v2 (commit 897fac9) -- Grade: A-

Major redesign. This no longer looks like a web toolbar. It looks like it belongs in a game.

What changed:

  • Warm amber palette (HUD constant object with panelBg, panelBorder, panelInnerGlow, etc.). Colors: #120E0A base, rgba(255,183,77) amber accents. This connects visually to the warm light in the full-office image.
  • 34px agent portraits with SVG status rings instead of 20px dots. Active agents get a pulsing radial glow behind their portrait. Full sprite images, clipped circular. This IS the Sims household panel.
  • Rounded top corners (12px) with 8px side margins on desktop. The panel "sits" at the bottom rather than spanning edge-to-edge. More like a game panel / piece of furniture than a toolbar.
  • SVG noise texture overlay at 1.5% opacity. Subtle but adds materiality. The panel has texture, not flat glass.
  • "Today" project card gets a flame icon and an orange left accent bar. Visual urgency without being obnoxious.
  • Project cards have bottom progress fills (2px colored bar at the bottom edge) instead of inline progress bars. Cleaner.
  • 58px height on desktop (was 48px). The extra 10px accommodates the larger 34px portraits without feeling cramped.
  • Expanded task panel has warm inner glow at top (amber gradient), staggered entry animations on individual tasks (via motion.div with delay indexed to position), warm-themed scrollbar.

What's working (Sims x Chaart x Indie Game test):

  • Sims: Agent portraits with status rings. Check. Household panel energy. Check.
  • Chaart: Clean data density with project cards, progress, and stats cluster. Check.
  • Indie Game: Warm palette, noise texture, rounded game-panel shape, flame icon. Check.
  • The baby IS born. This HUD doesn't look like any existing dashboard framework. It looks like its own thing.

What's NOT working:

Z-INDEX COLLISION STILL PRESENT. GameHUD at bottom:0 (z:40), ChatBar at bottom:0 (z:30). On desktop, the HUD's 58px completely covers the ChatBar's 56px. This is the critical bug from Pass 2 and it's unchanged. The HUD redesign is gorgeous but the chat is hidden behind it.

Agent portraits may feel small at 34px on large monitors. 34px is right for 1080p but might feel tiny on 4K. Consider a responsive size: 34px up to 1440p, 42px above. Not urgent.

Production fallback still shows "No task data." Same issue from Pass 2. The warm empty state ("No task data" in amber tones) is marginally better than the v1 empty state, but still needs demo data for production.

Grade rationale: A- because the visual design is excellent and it solves the "doesn't feel like a game" problem. Docked for the z-index collision (critical UX bug) and empty production state.

9. CHATBAR v2 + SPEAKING WIRE COMPLETE (commit a5bc5f2) -- Grade: A-

Bobby closed the loop on three items from my report in one commit.

Chat-to-sprite state: WIRED.

  • ChatBar now calls setSpeaking(true/false) which calls onSpeaking(agentSlug, isSpeaking) up to the parent.
  • Parent sets streamingAgent state and passes it to IsometricOffice.
  • IsometricOffice renders a speech bubble with 3 bouncing typing dots over the room when streamingAgent === room.id.
  • The bubble uses framer-motion spring animation (stiffness 400, damping 20) for a lively entrance.
  • CSS keyframe chatTypingDot with staggered delays (0s, 0.15s, 0.3s) for the dot bounce.
  • Speech bubble tail (CSS triangle) pointing down from the bubble to the room.

This is the first time the chat and the isometric world are visually connected. When you chat with Elon, Elon's room shows the typing dots. The building responds to your interaction. This is a core product differentiator.

Smooth auto-scroll.

  • scrollToBottom(instant) method uses scrollTo({ behavior: instant ? 'instant' : 'smooth' }).
  • User messages scroll instantly (you don't want to wait for your own message to appear).
  • Assistant messages scroll smoothly (lets you see the response streaming in).
  • Uses messagesContainerRef instead of messagesEndRef.scrollIntoView. More reliable.

Auto-expand on send.

  • If the chat is collapsed when you hit send, it automatically expands. You don't have to manually open the chat to see the response. Small but important UX detail.

Timestamp formatting.

  • formatTime() function: "just now", "Nm ago", or HH:MM AM/PM for older messages. Human-readable.

Speaking state lifecycle is clean:

  1. User sends message -> setSpeaking(true) -> parent gets onSpeaking(agentSlug, true) -> streamingAgent = agentSlug -> bubble appears over room
  2. Response received (relay poll) -> setSpeaking(false) -> parent gets onSpeaking(agentSlug, false) -> streamingAgent = null -> bubble disappears
  3. Error -> setSpeaking(false) -> same cleanup

What's NOT working:

  • The speech bubble appears on the static image, positioned at bottom: '55%', left: '50%' of the room target div. This works but the position is approximate. On some rooms the bubble might overlap the nameplate. Per-room bubble offsets would be more precise.
  • The speaking animation only shows typing dots. The spec's RPG dialogue vision ("response streams in word by word in a speech bubble") isn't here yet. But the current implementation is a solid foundation for that.

11. WHAT IT TAKES TO HIT A (Updated)

Three items remain. Priority order:

  1. Fix z-index collision. GameHUD (z:40, bottom:0, 58px) covers ChatBar (z:30, bottom:0, 56px) on desktop. This is the ONLY critical bug. Fix: set ChatBar to bottom:58 (or merge them). 5 minutes. This has been flagged since Pass 2.

  2. Per-room WORKING glow. When an agent is WORKING, their room's click-target div should show a subtle radial gradient in the agent's color at 10-15% opacity. The click targets already exist. Add a conditional background. 20 lines.

  3. Production demo data. Hard-code 4-5 project cards with sample tasks for non-localhost. The HUD looks great when data is present. Show it off.

Those three items turn B+ into A. Everything else (RPG chat style, 2048px image, per-room bubble offsets) is polish.

12. VIEWPORT-FILL + WAVE LOAD + CLIP PATHS (commit 1f669da) -- Quick Review

Bobby keeps shipping. Three micro-improvements in this commit:

Viewport-filling building. IMG_SIZE is now dynamic: Math.max(containerWidth, containerHeight, 880) * 1.15. The building fills the screen with no dead space. The 1.15 multiplier means the image slightly exceeds viewport bounds, so when you zoom to 1.0x the building bleeds off-screen naturally rather than floating in a void. This is the Crossy Road energy: the world extends beyond your view.

Wave load-in animation. ROOM_WAVE_ORDER defines a center-outward sequence: main-hall first, then radiating to corners. Each room gets delay: index * 0.06s. Total animation time: ~0.8s for all 14 rooms. This makes the office "wake up" when you load the page. Good micro-interaction.

Isometric clip-path polygons. Each room's click target now has a CSS clip-path hexagon (polygon(50% 0%, 100% 25%, 100% 75%, 50% 100%, 0% 75%, 0% 25%)) instead of a rectangular hit area. This prevents misclicks near room edges where isometric rooms share borders. Smart detail.

Does this change the grade? Visual Composition moves from B+ to borderline A-. The building fills the viewport naturally, loads with personality, and has precision click areas. The only things keeping it from A are: (a) no per-room glow for WORKING state, and (b) the static image doesn't change with agent state. Both are solvable within the current architecture.

OVERALL: B+ HEADING TO A

Bobby shipped 8 commits in under 20 minutes. The product went from C+ (isolated rooms on a grid) to B+ (viewport-filling cohesive building with warm game HUD, live chat wiring, speaking sprites, wave animations). That's the fastest grade improvement I've seen.

The A-grade gap is now just 3 items:

  1. Z-index collision fix (5 min, critical bug)
  2. Per-room WORKING glow (20 lines)
  3. Production demo data

When those land, this is an A. The architecture, visual design, and product vision alignment are all there.

PASS 4: PLAYWRIGHT LIVE TESTING (Patrik's New Directives)

Test method: Playwright headless browser against localhost:5173/dashboard. 14 automated tests. Screenshots captured at every step.

Patrik's critical directives tested against:

  1. Projects ranked by RECENCY and FREQUENCY of conversation, not static order
  2. Real chat with each agent on localhost must actually work
  3. Checklist needs ordered tasks per project with sexy filtering
  4. HUD and context are ONE
  5. Click and test EVERYTHING continuously

13. LIVE TESTING ANALYSIS: Grading Against Patrik's Vision

The core test: "Can Patrik manage his day from this in 30 seconds?"

Result: 5/8 vitals visible on fresh load.

Vital Present? Notes
Active agents YES Agent sprites on building with status dots.
Blocked agents NO No BLOCKED status text visible on initial view. Status dots exist but no explicit "blocked" call-out.

Urgent items NO No ASAP/overdue/RED call-outs in game mode.
